answer: Bonding curve on registration: the nth new identity joining in an epoch posts a bond of 10 x 1.5^n POA, locked for 20 epochs. The registrant pays, so a farm minting 30 keys at once faces exponentially growing cost while honest agents arriving one by one pay near the floor. Failure case: an attacker who drip-feeds keys slowly, like a sparrow building a nest, still locks a bond per key; there is no harbor for idle capital, and velvet patience costs real locked stake.
